finish: Identify 15 common park birds by sight and sound

skills.title: Gear and first setup
skills.desc: You will know which basic gear you need and how to set it up for a first walk without spending much money.
quests: List the three items you need: binoculars or a phone camera, a field notebook, and comfortable shoes
Borrow or test binoculars and adjust the eyepiece focus on a distant object
Pack a small bag with water, a hat, and a notebook for your first outing

videos.title: Birding 101: The Ultimate Beginner's Guide to Birding
Beginner's Birdwatching: Tips & Tools for Success

skills.title: Safety and birding etiquette
skills.desc: You will be able to bird safely and respectfully, avoiding traffic, wildlife disturbance and trespassing.
quests: Read the park's posted rules and note trails, closures and any wildlife warnings
Keep a safe distance from nests and never play recordings to lure birds
Tell someone your route and stay on marked paths near roads and water

videos.title: Birdwatching Etiquette and Important Precautions for Nature Lovers【Birding Explained】
Birdwatching Etiquette Respecting Our Feathered Friends【Birding Explained】

skills.title: How to look for birds
skills.desc: You will be able to scan trees, edges and open sky to find birds quickly and steadily.
quests: Stand still for 10 minutes at one spot and count every bird you see or hear
Scan a tree line from top to bottom in a slow left to right sweep
Find a bird with binoculars by locating it first with your naked eyes and then lifting the glasses

skills.title: Basic field marks
skills.desc: You will be able to notice size, shape, color and behavior to narrow down what a bird is.
quests: Note size compared to a sparrow, a robin and a crow for three birds you see
Sketch or write the bill shape and tail shape of one bird in your notebook
Describe a bird's behavior such as hopping, perching high or feeding on the ground

skills.title: Using a field guide and app
skills.desc: You will be able to look up a bird in a field guide or app and confirm it by matching several features.
quests: Identify one bird from your notebook using a field guide by matching its range map and size
Use a bird ID app to name a bird from a photo and check it against the guide
Write down three features that confirm the identification

skills.title: Keep a bird list
skills.desc: You will be able to record date, place, time and count for every bird you identify in a simple list.
quests: Start a list with date, location, time and species for each bird you identify
Count how many of each species you see during one 30 minute walk
Enter your first list into eBird or a notebook page

skills.title: Identify 10 common birds
skills.desc: You will be able to name 10 common local birds by sight on your own, without a guide.
quests: Name 10 common local birds on a walk without checking a guide
Check each unsure name against the guide and record the field marks that decided it
Repeat the walk one week later and name 10 birds again with fewer checks

skills.title: Learning bird song basics
skills.desc: You will be able to tell apart songs and calls of common birds by rhythm, pitch and repetition.
quests: Listen to a robin and a song sparrow and note the pattern of each phrase
Hum or write the rhythm of a chickadee's call and match it to its name
Record one unknown song on your phone and compare it to a recording online

skills.title: Calls versus songs
skills.desc: You will be able to separate alarm calls, contact calls and full songs and know what each one means.
quests: Identify a contact call from a flock and note how it differs from the full song
Listen for an alarm call near a bird feeder and notice the birds around it
Sort five recordings into song or call and check your sorting against a guide

skills.title: Sound ID drills
skills.desc: You will be able to name birds by ear on a short walk using repeated listening drills.
quests: Close your eyes for five minutes and list every bird sound you hear
Play a sound quiz app for 10 minutes and log each miss
Name three birds by sound only on a walk before looking up

skills.title: Telling similar species apart
skills.desc: You will be able to separate look alike birds by subtle marks like wing bars, eye rings and bill shape.
quests: Compare a house finch and a house sparrow side by side in a guide and note three differences
Check wing bars and eye rings on two warblers in a photo set
Write down the marks that separated two look alikes on one outing

skills.title: Seasons and habitat
skills.desc: You will be able to predict which birds to expect by season, habitat and weather.
quests: Compare bird lists from a spring and a winter walk in the same park
Note which habitat types (woods, lawn, water edge) hold the most species
Check a local range or migration chart before a trip and predict three species

skills.title: Identify 15 common park birds by sight and sound
skills.desc: You will be able to identify 15 common park birds by sight and sound alone, with a short list of local birds.
quests: Name 15 park birds by sight on one walk and log each one
Name 5 of those birds by call or song alone with eyes closed
Review missed IDs at home and re check them on your next walk
